title: Bag of tricks: synergistic optimization of deep patch learning fuzzy systems with multi-strategy integration
task: Optimize deep patch learning fuzzy systems for classification via structural tuning
key_results: Proposed bag-of-tricks integration (feature combination, drop connect, subsystem deletion) synergistically enhances DPFSCAs classification performance; addresses exponential rule growth (e.g., 59,049 rules for 10D inputs) and numerical instability (trigger strength ≤0.00098)
comments: Practical structural optimization approach for fuzzy systems; multi-strategy synergism demonstrated empirically but lacks theoretical analysis of why individual techniques combine effectively.

model_io.model: Deep Patch Learning Fuzzy Systems for Classification (DPFSCAs)
Optimization techniques: Feature Combination (FC), Drop Connect (DC), Subsystem Deletion (SD)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Structural optimization via FC, DC, and SD reduces exponential rule growth and improves stability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; synergistic effects of combined techniques enhance performance on diverse datasets

title: Performance evaluation of tunicate-enhanced NGO resource optimization in RF energy harvesting–assisted NOMA edge computing
task: Optimize RF energy harvesting in NOMA edge computing for IoT farms
key_results: TNGO algorithm minimizes delay outage probability by optimizing time switching factor, power allocation coefficient, and task allocation ratio under Rayleigh fading with imperfect CSI
comments: Application-driven optimization study combining bio-inspired algorithms with communication systems; practical relevance for constrained IoT devices but limited theoretical novelty.

hypotheses.hypothesis: TNGO can find optimal parameters to minimize delay outage probability in RFE-NOMA-MEC systems
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; TNGO outperforms baseline methods with optimal parameter utilization

title: A data-driven geographic information system and machine learning based multi-criteria framework for strategic wind power plant siting
task: Select optimal wind farm sites integrating GIS, expert judgment, efficiency analysis, and ML predictions
key_results: Integrated FAHP-DEA-ML framework identifies 1,698 km² high-priority corridors in North Shewa; Random Forest achieved RMSE=0.2981, R²=0.8145 (regression) and F1=0.9207, accuracy=0.9237 (classification) with independent validation via 250 MW project pipeline
comments: Well-structured multi-stage framework combining fuzzy weighting, DEA efficiency screening, and predictive ML; strong practical validation but wind speed dominance (0.4211) may limit generalizability to other regions.

inputs: expert judgment on 6 criteria (wind speed, slope, elevation, transmission distance, road distance, LULC)

model_io.model: Machine Learning ensemble (Random Forest, SVM, XGBoost)

hypotheses.hypothesis: Integration of FAHP, DEA, and ML improves site selection beyond static GIS approaches
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; framework delineates actionable corridors validated against government pipeline projects

title: Critical oscillation characteristics of fluidic oscillators operating with power-law fluids
task: Characterize oscillation onset in fluidic oscillators with non-Newtonian power-law fluids
key_results: Critical threshold identified at n≈0.61 (K≈0.163) where Coanda effect fails; expansion angle >20° suppresses oscillation; two locking states identified (marginal vs. deep)
comments: Rigorous numerical investigation revealing coupled rheology-geometry effects; practical constraints on fluidic component design with complex fluids are well-characterized.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Consistency index K and flow behavior index n strongly couple to determine oscillation onset
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; critical threshold n≈0.61 identified as decisive bifurcation point

hypotheses.hypothesis: Expansion angle α suppresses oscillation stability
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; angles >20° accelerate flow degradation under shear-thinning conditions

title: A novel quantum motivated particle swarm method with enhanced search strategy for electromagnetic optimization problems
task: Optimize electromagnetic design parameters using quantum-inspired particle swarm optimization
key_results: Proposed SQPSO achieves faster convergence, higher-quality solutions, and improved robustness against local optima compared to existing metaheuristics on benchmark and electromagnetic applications
comments: Standard metaheuristic enhancement combining probability-based mutation, tournament selection, and dynamic parameters; effectiveness demonstrated empirically but lacks theoretical convergence analysis.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Probability-based mutation and tournament selection improve exploration-exploitation balance in PSO
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; SQPSO achieves faster convergence and stronger robustness than baseline methods

title: Rethinking scale in ophthalmic artificial intelligence: from bigger models to smarter clinical reasoning
task: Advance ophthalmic AI toward trustworthy clinical reasoning beyond model scaling
key_results: Argues for shift from benchmark-driven scaling toward multimodal integration, external knowledge incorporation, and uncertainty quantification in clinical AI systems
comments: Position paper identifying important gap between benchmark performance and clinical deployment; lacks empirical validation of proposed principles.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Clinical trust in ophthalmic AI requires integration of multimodal evidence, external knowledge, and uncertainty reasoning rather than model/data scaling alone
hypotheses.result: Proposed framework; validation pending through real-world clinical trials

title: Geometry of the cumulant series in diffusion MRI
task: Establish hardware-independent diffusion MRI fingerprint via cumulant tensor invariants
key_results: All kurtosis invariants improve MS classification (1189-subject cohort); icosahedral 1–2 minute acquisitions determine key invariants; scalar invariant maps enable fast clinical protocols
comments: The SO(3) symmetry-based invariant analysis is mathematically rigorous, but clinical translation requires validation against multiple pathologies beyond MS.

model_io.model: Rotational SO(3) symmetric analysis of dMRI cumulant tensors
inputs: tissue diffusion structure at micron scale

hypotheses.hypothesis: Including all kurtosis invariants improves MS classification
Icosahedral sampling optimally determines key invariants in 1–2 minutes

title: Decoupling capacitive sensing from circuit knowledge via time-domain representation
task: Develop hardware-independent capacitive sensor readout framework
key_results: Time-domain framework eliminates need for absolute capacitance extraction; two-point temporal anchoring corrects circuit variations; validated across three sensor types with diverse hardware
comments: Shifting from capacitance-centric to time-domain representation is elegant, though the generalizability to sensors with fundamentally different transduction mechanisms remains to be demonstrated.

model_io.model: Time-domain capacitive sensing framework with microcontroller threshold voltage

hypotheses.hypothesis: Circuit variations manifest primarily as time-axis scaling
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; correctable via two-point anchoring without recalibration

hypotheses.hypothesis: Framework is platform-independent across different sensor designs
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; consistent responses recovered across non-contact, commercial, and displacement sensors

title: Pharmacological markers of HIV prevention for oral pre-exposure prophylaxis in men who have sex with men
task: Determine tissue-level pharmacokinetic markers predictive of oral PrEP efficacy in MSM
key_results: PBMC-based predictions align with clinical PrEP efficacy in MSM; rectal tissue pharmacokinetics do not predict efficacy (sufficient power in HPTN 083, DISCOVER trials); adherence requirements likely similar between women and MSM
comments: This mechanistic PK-efficacy approach elegantly decouples tissue exposure from clinical protection, suggesting that intracellular drug concentrations rather than local mucosal levels drive prevention outcomes.

model_io.model: Mechanistic PK-efficacy model with tissue-specific pharmacokinetic matrices
outputs: predicted PrEP efficacy by tissue compartment

hypotheses.hypothesis: Rectal tissue pharmacokinetics predict oral PrEP efficacy in MSM
hypotheses.result: Rejected; HPTN 083 and DISCOVER trials show rectal PK does not correlate with clinical efficacy

hypotheses.hypothesis: PBMC pharmacokinetics predict PrEP efficacy in MSM
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; PBMC-based predictions agree with clinical efficacy observations

title: Modelling the impact of climate on cholera: a case study of Kolkata
task: Project cholera incidence under future climate scenarios using mechanistic transmission models
key_results: Best model recreates seasonal patterns effectively; projects 81-150% increase in cholera cases by 2080-2099; contact rate and water dynamics parameters have greatest impact on projections
comments: While mechanistic models offer advantages over statistical approaches, projections remain constrained by critical knowledge gaps in epidemiological parameters and temperature-dependent bacterial growth rates.

model_io.model: Four mechanistic cholera transmission models with varying climate sensitivity assumptions

hypotheses.hypothesis: Temperature and rainfall jointly explain cholera seasonality better than either alone
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; dual-input model recreates seasonal patterns highly effectively

hypotheses.hypothesis: Climate change will increase future cholera burden in Kolkata
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; average 81-150% increase projected with earlier seasonal peaks
